name: Isaiah
description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Isaiah answered, thus saith the Lord: be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Hezekiah falls sick unto death, and Isaiah brings the word to set his house in order, for he shall die and not live.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Isaiah applies a lump of figs to the boil and Hezekiah recovers, showing that remedies and herbs go together with prayer, for healing is in the hand of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Isaiah cries to the Most High and He brings the shadow ten degrees backward on the dial of Ahaz, reversing the natural course of the sun as proof of His power.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Isaiah asks what the men saw and where they came from, then declares that all in the house shall be carried into Babylon, and Hezekiah's own sons shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amos, pray and cry to heaven over this railing.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerns Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. These are the days in which Isaiah prophesied.

Isaiah was a servant and prophet during Hezekiah's reign, before the Assyrian captivity destroyed the nation. The split between the northern and southern kingdoms had already come, going back to Solomon's idolatry and the friction between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
Isaiah is a heavy, prophetic book; even the Ethiopian eunuch was reading Isaiah when the spirit sent Philip to help him understand it.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: The Most High told Isaiah to go meet Ahaz, he and his son Shearjashub, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the highway of the fuller's field.

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

points: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see. When it says the burden of Babylon, the burden goes into the destruction or judgment God is going to bring on Babylon. So Isaiah saw the judgment of Babylon.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see. The Lord sent him a vision.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: He told Isaiah to loose the sackcloth from his loins and put off his shoe from his foot, and Isaiah did so, walking naked and barefoot.

note.label: Isaiah 20: Naked and Barefoot for a Sign

points: He sends Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet. He calls it a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: This is exactly what happened: Sennacherib was killed in his own land by his own sons, showing the word of the Most High through Isaiah came to pass. No nation can stand against Israel when the Most High has spoken against it.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Isaiah answers the servants: tell your master, Be not afraid of the words with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me. The Most High answers the blasphemy directly.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: In those days Hezekiah was sick unto death, and Isaiah the son of Amoz came and told him to set his house in order, for he would die and not live. Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, reminding the Most High how he had walked before him in truth and with a perfect heart, and he wept sore.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: Isaiah had said to take a lump of figs and lay it as a plaster upon the boil that he might recover, and Hezekiah had asked what the sign was that he should go up to the house of the Lord.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, is Isaiah's word spoken of John.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: In them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias: by hearing ye shall hear and shall not understand, and seeing ye shall see and shall not perceive.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

points: John preaches the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, as it is written in the book of the words of Esaias: the voice of one crying in the wilderness.

note.label: Luke 3: The Preaching of John and the Generations Back to Adam

points: The book delivered to him was Isaiah, and the place he found was Isaiah 61.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

points: These things said Esaias when he saw his glory, and spake of him: the glory Isaiah saw was Christ's.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

cases.name: Isaiah
cases.charge: Here am I; send me: a prophet unto a people whose heart was made fat, who walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign, and stood beside the king when Assyria blasphemed
cases.preview: In the year king Uzziah died Isaiah saw the Lord on His throne, confessed himself a man of unclean lips, was cleansed by a coal from the altar, and answered the call to go (Isaiah 6:1-8).
